mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls >10% q/q
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent surge in personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) signals a liquidity trap environment, which depresses risk asset valuations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1 flat) signals a savings glut, which reduces current demand and leads to flat or negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >0.3% m/m AND GDPC1 change ≈ 0% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) to below 50k new jobs per month for two consecutive months, despite a stable unemployment rate, signals hidden labor market slack, which precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not negative (< -0.2%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.
